basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Crevit igitur puer et ablactatus est, fecitque Abraham grande convivium in die'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Crevit igitur puer et ablactatus est, fecitque Abraham grande convivium in die ablactationis ejus. Lacte nutritur Isaac cum electus quisque, filius videlicet promissionis, nuper in Christo genitus, prima fidei rudimenta suscipit, et quamvis necdum summa divinitatis arcana scrutari sufficit, dulcedine tamen praemiorum coelestium delectatus, bonis insistere operibus contendit, per quae Deo adjuvante largienteque potiora capere mereatur, juxta illud apostoli Petri: Deponentes igitur omnem malitiam, et omnem dolum, et simulationes, et invidias, et omnes detractiones, sicut modo geniti infantes, rationabile et sine dolo lac concupiscite, ut in eo crescatis in salutem, si tamen gustastis quoniam dulcis est Dominus. Sed ablactatus Isaac atque ad panis edulium pervenit, cum electi proficientibus fidei incrementis non solum Jesum Christum, et hunc crucifixum confiteri discunt, verum etiam addere quia in principio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum.
